_schema._lee_esto_primero: Este bloque documenta el formato y no es dato de la app. Se conserva en cada export para que el esquema viaje con el archivo: quien lo consuma no necesita buscar otro documento. Las apps que adopten este formato copian este bloque tal cual y rellenan el resto.
_schema._origen: Definido por app-dash-agent-ai en su entrega de brochure (2026-08-19). Es el PRIMER export del portafolio; las demás apps lo adoptan.
_schema._consumidor: La vitrina de hoja-de-vida. Renderiza la ficha de cada app sin abrir su repositorio.
_schema._regla_madre: Toda cifra de `metricas[]` lleva su etiqueta de `fuente`. Es la regla dura 3 de Dash Agent AI aplicada a su propia ficha: una app que exige procedencia a cada número de su pantalla no puede publicar cifras sueltas sobre sí misma. Se recomienda al resto del portafolio.
_schema.schema_version: semver del FORMATO, no de la app. Cambio mayor = campo eliminado o con significado distinto; menor = campo nuevo opcional; parche = documentación.
_schema.app.estado: "inicial" mientras el brochure describe la construcción cerrada; "sellado" cuando el gate de pruebas del usuario terminó. `sellado_en` es null hasta entonces.
_schema.funcionalidades.total: El número que el brochure declara en su pie. `fuente_del_conteo` dice contra qué documento se cuadró — sin eso, el total es una afirmación.
_schema.funcionalidades.descartadas: Las que se construyeron o se planearon y NO existen. Van aquí con su razón y su fecha para que nadie las cuente como pendientes ni como entregadas.
_schema.metricas[].fuente: Una de cuatro: "medido" (salió de un contador o un comando), "calculada" (medido operado con una tarifa o una regla, y se dice cuál), "declarado" (lo fijó una persona), "estimacion" (deducido). Una cifra sin fuente no entra.
_schema.enlaces.produccion: null cuando la app no tiene URL pública. `razon` explica por qué, y es lo que la vitrina muestra en lugar del enlace. Nunca se rellena con un enlace de repositorio ni con una promesa.

promesa.tagline: Your AI agent, measured against the plan you wrote before building it.
promesa.intro: planlang turns the plan of an AI-agent project into a verifiable contract: what the agent decides, what can go wrong, what is taken for granted and how success is measured. With that contract the agent is built, run on hundreds of cases whose answer is known, and the gap between what was planned and what happened is published, failures included, in a static showcase that calls no model.
promesa.para_quien: For whoever plans, builds or approves AI agents and today judges them by reading traces and running loose evaluations, without having written down first what they were meant to do. Whoever decides gets a verdict in plain words; whoever builds gets the rule, the signal and the case behind every figure.
promesa.diferencial: Of 15 evaluation platforms reviewed in September 2026, none requires planning before building or compares the plan with what happened. planlang does both: it demands a measurable plan, publishes the gap between plan and result with the risks that were foreseen, and lets you move the plan's thresholds over the agent's real decisions.

grupos.linea: You write what the agent decides, what can fail and how it is measured; an incomplete plan does not pass.

features.nombre: Start with what your sector requires
features.que_hace: You start the plan with the actors, risks and criteria typical of health, finance or AI security, with the legal constraints in plain language and their source. Adding a new sector means adding a data file, without touching code.

features.nombre: No half-finished plan gets through
features.que_hace: You know before building whether your plan can be measured. A validator with no AI rejects, with the exact reason, criteria without a rule, thresholds without a signal and serious risks without mitigation. The approved plan is sealed with a fingerprint that exposes any later change.

features.nombre: An interviewer that drafts your plan
features.que_hace: You answer questions in order, each with an example, and get the draft of your plan in Spanish and English. Before handing it over, it points out what is missing and the contradictions. It never approves for you: that signature is yours.

features.nombre: Plan a real project, not only the demos
features.que_hace: The interviewer walks through the sector template for any project and, when you approve it, the plan is published in the showcase as a contract that states what it does not have yet: traces, gap and playground. The first one was HackGuard's two agents.

features.nombre: The plan is the code that decides
features.que_hace: What the agent decides is literally what the plan says. The plan fixes its pieces, every step rule as signal, operator and value (for example, “confidence below 0.75”), where a person decides and what every case must record.

grupos.nombre: Test with cases whose answer is known
grupos.linea: Two demos with real agents run on hundreds of invented cases whose correct answer is already known.

features.nombre: Cases whose answer is already known
features.que_hace: You test the agent on invented batches whose correct answer is already known: normal cases, edge cases, incomplete ones and traps such as hidden instructions or similar names. Generating them again gives the same cases, and a validator blocks any data shaped like real data.

features.nombre: Demo A: medical authorizations
features.que_hace: You watch a team of agents decide 200 medical authorization requests: approve, approve up to the covered cap, deny with a legal ground or hand the case to an auditor. Emergencies are authorized without checking coverage, and no full denial goes out without a person.

features.nombre: Demo B: onboarding with due diligence
features.que_hace: You watch the agents decide whether a client is onboarded: they read the documents, search watchlists, investigate similar names and score risk by rules, without protected attributes. Every rejection and every high risk goes through the compliance officer.

features.nombre: A case file that cites its sources
features.que_hace: Every demo B request ends in a case file in Spanish and English written by code, not by the AI. Each conclusion cites the plan's rule or the watchlist match, with its version and date.

features.nombre: Every denial, explained and appealable
features.que_hace: If the agent denies a service, even in part, a document in Spanish and English is produced by code: the legal ground, the rule applied, the data used, who decided and how to contest the decision.

features.nombre: Knows who stands behind a company
features.que_hace: When the applicant is a company, the agent copies its ownership structure and AI-free code works out who the beneficial owners are: 25% or more, direct or through chains of companies, and whoever controls it, with exact arithmetic. If the structure does not add up, it does not guess: it sends it to a person.

features.nombre: Batch runs, without losing a case
features.que_hace: You run hundreds of cases with the Claude Code subscription, 20 at a time and with pauses. If the run is cut off, it resumes where it stopped without repeating any, and every case leaves its trace, every decision with its signal, in a format of its own and with a fingerprint.

grupos.nombre: Measure the gap, with no AI in between
grupos.linea: A verifier with no AI compares what was planned with what happened and also publishes what failed.

features.nombre: The gap report: plan against reality
features.que_hace: You know, criterion by criterion and risk by risk, what was met and in which cases it was not. A verifier that uses no AI reads the plan and what the agent did, and writes the report in Spanish and English, identical every time it is repeated.

features.nombre: Assumptions put to the test
features.que_hace: What the plan took for granted without testing is measured and ends up confirmed, refuted or untested. In demo A two fell: two clarifications were not enough, and several agents turned out slower than a single one.

features.nombre: Several agents against a single one
features.que_hace: You put the team of agents against a single agent, with the same plan and the same 200 cases, and compare accuracy, time, cost and differing cases. In demo A the team was more accurate (98% against 90%) but slower.

features.nombre: A gauge that is also gauged
features.que_hace: planlang tests its own yardstick. It planted 10 failures on purpose and the verifier found every one, with no false alarms. It also redid the agents' 1,204 decisions in another programming language, with zero differences.
features.seccion_manual: Check the runs and the instrument

features.nombre: How much the data backs a threshold
features.que_hace: The agent's confidence comes with its guarantee: the lowest threshold whose error, among what the agent decides alone, stays under the one you accept with the probability you set. If the data does not reach it, the report says so and how many cases it would take.

features.nombre: The legal deadline, measured
features.que_hace: A simulated clock and an auditor over the traces that already exist say whether each authorization was decided within its legal deadline: the wait of each class, the late ones by case and where the deadline breaks, even if that is outside what the playground lets you move. Without rerunning a case.

features.nombre: The underlying rules, in writing
features.que_hace: Everything that can be solved with code is solved without AI, and every piece of the agent that uses no model says why. Using the Claude Code subscription was decided in writing, with its terms reread before each delivery.
features.seccion_manual: Check the runs and the instrument

grupos.nombre: Move a threshold, see what changes
grupos.linea: You try other plan values over the agent's real decisions, without calling the model again.

features.nombre: Move the plan's thresholds
features.que_hace: You change a threshold, such as minimum confidence or Texas mode, which sends every denial to a person, even a partial one, and you see which cases change path, which errors appear and how much human work it costs. Everything is recomputed in your browser, with no model.

features.nombre: Move the auditor's capacity
features.que_hace: You change how many requests the auditor handles per business day and see how many go past their legal deadline, by class, and how many auditor hours it costs, with the thresholds you are playing. It is recomputed in your browser, with the same clock as the report.

grupos.linea: The diagram comes from the code that ran and flags any piece the plan requires that is missing.

features.nombre: The agent, as it ran
features.que_hace: You see the agent's diagram generated from the code that ran, not drawn by hand. You tap a piece and it shows what it does, its code and the real cases that went through it; if something the plan requires is missing, the diagram flags it.

grupos.nombre: Walk through it in the browser
grupos.linea: planlang's showcase: a bilingual, serverless site read as a leader or as an expert.

features.nombre: The idea on one screen
features.que_hace: You understand right away why planning matters: according to a LangChain survey, 89% of teams observe their agents and 52% evaluate them, but the survey does not even ask whether they planned what to evaluate. Below, the method in three steps and what was measured.

features.nombre: Each demo, end to end
features.que_hace: You walk through each demo in six screens: plan, agent, gap, playground, cases and records, in Spanish or English, in light or dark theme and from your phone. You read as a leader, in plain words, or as an expert, with the rule behind every figure.

features.nombre: Repeatable and ready for the Portfolio
features.que_hace: Every run comes with its record so the same report can be obtained again: versions, fingerprints, seed, model and date. The app also builds its own record and the static package the Portfolio publishes, with no link at all and with the fingerprint of every file.

metricas.etiqueta: criteria met across the plans of 2 demos, of 18
metricas.detalle: Demo A: 11 of 11, in verifier 1.5.0's report on run suscripcion-planlang-a-002-200-v1.5. Demo B: 6 of 7, in verifier 1.5.0's report on run suscripcion-planlang-b-002-20.

metricas.etiqueta: decisions redone in another language, with 0 differences
metricas.detalle: RF-09.2 cross-check over 4 runs of 2 demos: the TypeScript edge interpreter redoes every decision Python recorded.

metricas.etiqueta: synthetic cases with a known answer, across 2 demos
metricas.detalle: Demo A: 200 cases in run suscripcion-planlang-a-002-200-v1.5 and the single-agent baseline. Demo B: 20 cases in run suscripcion-planlang-b-002-20 and the single-agent baseline.

metricas.etiqueta: model calls when visiting the showcase
metricas.detalle: Set by the architecture: the showcase is a static export with precomputed data; the package is tested without a single request outside its origin.

metricas.etiqueta: nominal cost of running each demo once (220 cases)
metricas.detalle: Demo A: US$ 4.9206 for 200 cases. Demo B: US$ 0.2465 for 20 cases. Sum of the nominal cost the CLI declares per call, over each run's traces; through the subscription it was not paid separately.

The product vision's features that work today: the two-week cut's and the roadmap ones built in S3 (the interviewer, demo B and its case file), counted against docs/MANUAL-DE-USO.md; what remains on the roadmap does not count.

stack.papel: the showcase: seven screens in Spanish and English, no server
the deterministic core: plan, verifier, playground and viewer, the same in Node and in the browser
both demos' agents, with the human pause as an interrupt
the agents' model, in batches outside CI; never in the core or the showcase
plans, cases, traces and reports with a fingerprint, checkable byte for byte
the tests, including the edge cross-check between Python and TypeScript

privacidad.detalle: Everything is synthetic and comes from a seeded generator: cases, members, physicians, benefit plans, applicants and watchlists. On every change, an automated validator rejects any identifier with a real-looking form. The showcase is static: whoever visits it triggers no call to a model or to any external service.

enlaces.razon: planlang has no public address of its own: its showcase travels to the Portfolio as a static package, labeled “Simulation · not operational”, and is walked through there.
enlaces.razon_repositorio: The repository is not linked: the Portfolio publishes no access links, by house rule.
enlaces.brochure_archivo: no file of its own: the showcase and its records serve as the brochure (sprint 3 decision)
enlaces.brochure_ruta_local: no /conoce route: the showcase is the app's presentation (sprint 3 decision)
